cases.customer_question: What information and materials are required before an RF two-item Bluetooth test plan can be created and testing can proceed?
question_variants: What must be submitted for RF2 testing?
What is needed to prepare a Bluetooth RF test plan?
Can RF testing begin before IXIT/ICS information is provided?
What documents should accompany a Bluetooth RF test sample shipment?
What inputs are required for RF qualification planning?
cases.actual_issue: RF qualification testing requires receipt of the test sample and supporting qualification information before the laboratory can generate the RF test plan and begin testing.
cases.plain_english_explanation: The customer wanted to send a product for Bluetooth RF testing. Before testing can start, the laboratory needs the device, operational instructions, and qualification-related information used to build the test plan. Without those inputs, the lab cannot properly prepare or execute the RF test scope.
cases.consultant_answer: The laboratory requested shipment of the test sample together with an equipment-submission form, operating instructions, and qualification information needed for test-plan generation. After the required information was received, an RF test plan was created using associated ICS/IXIT planning materials and stored for execution. The discussion shows that test-plan creation is a prerequisite activity before RF testing proceeds.
cases.decision_logic: Bluetooth RF testing depends on accurate test-plan generation. The test plan can only be prepared after receiving the implementation information, device-access details, and supporting documentation needed to determine the applicable RF test scope.
cases.final_recommendation: Collect and submit the test sample, equipment-submission documentation, operating instructions, and all qualification-planning information before requesting RF test execution. Generate and review the RF test plan prior to scheduling testing.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Missing planning inputs can delay test-plan creation, postpone RF testing, and require additional coordination before qualification activities can begin.
